newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh flood toll passes 100 mark.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh flood toll passes 100 mark.

text.p: Floods have killed at least 104 people in Bangladesh, including 19 who drowned after a boat capsized in a swollen river, officials and police said on Tuesday.
They said the 19 people missing for four days after the boat sank on the Sangu river were now believed to have drowned.
"We can no longer keep them on the missing list although their bodies have not been found yet. It's now certain that they have perished in the river," one official said.
Most of the other victims died in landslides and house cave-ins, police said. They said the death toll could rise further as detailed reports were awaited from many areas still cut off by the floods.
"Floodwaters have started receding in most of the 19 affected districts and we expect conditions to improve soon," one official said.
Meteorology officials said on Tuesday they did not expect further rainfall through the rest of the week.

Disater management officials said over 2.5 million people were affected by the floods, triggered by heavy monsoon rains. At least 250,000 were made homeless and 500,000 marooned in their partly submerged homes.
Agriculture officials said crops in 300,000 acres (120,000 hecrates) had been washed away. In addition, huge foodgrain stocks were damaged by floodwaters, they said, without giving exact estimates.
Besides crops, thousands of hectares of shrimp firms and other fish projects have been washed away, causing substantial damage, officials said.

"It's still early to assess the losses. But we guess total flood damage including crops, property and infrastucture would be no less than 10 billion taka ($229 million)," one official in Chittagong told Reuters.
Civil administration, army and airforce have geared up relief supplies to flood victims, who are facing an acute shortage of dry food, drinking water and medicine.
"The situation is most pressing in Chittagong, Cox's Bazar and the Chittagong Hill Tracts," one official said.
Some areas recovering from the floods faced new problems, including land and homes near river banks being eroded, officials said.
Medical teams have been sent to flood-swept areas to try to prevent diseases caused by people drinking polluted water and rotten food.
Road links in Chittagong, Cox's Bazar, Rangamati and Khagrachhari districts have been partially restored, officials in the Roads & Highways department said.
